headline: Voting Begins in First Regular BARMM Parliamentary Election
seoTitle: Voting Begins in First BARMM Parliamentary Election | FMB News
seoDescription: Early voting is underway in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the region holds its first regular parliamentary election on September 14, 2026.
deck: Priority voting opened at 5 a.m. for seniors, persons with disabilities and pregnant voters as the Bangsamoro region begins its first regular parliamentary election.
author: FMB News Desk
readerNote: This is a developing story. FMB News will update this report as verified information becomes available.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Voting has begun in the first regular parliamentary election of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao on Monday, September 14, 2026.

The Commission on Elections scheduled early voting from 5 a.m. to 7 a.m. for senior citizens, persons with disabilities and pregnant voters. Current Philippine reporting says that early-voting window is now open. Regular voting follows after the priority period.

Around 2.393 million registered voters are eligible to participate across the Bangsamoro region. Voters are choosing members of an 80-seat parliament through a mix of regional party, district and sectoral representation.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The election is a major step in the transition from the interim Bangsamoro Transition Authority to a parliament chosen directly through the region's electoral system.

The first regular parliamentary vote had been delayed and rescheduled before Republic Act No. 12317 fixed September 14, 2026 as election day. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. also declared the date a special non-working day in BARMM to allow residents to vote.

Comelec has said the election will use automated counting machines. GMA News reported 5,212 voting precincts across 105 municipalities and two cities, with the election filling 40 regional party seats, 32 district seats and eight sectoral seats.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The election is not only a regional political contest. It is tied directly to the Bangsamoro peace process and to the shift from an appointed transitional authority toward an elected parliamentary government.

Its conduct will be closely watched for turnout, security, credibility and whether the new system strengthens democratic institutions in a region shaped by decades of conflict, autonomy negotiations and political transition.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: Voting is still underway, so turnout, localized disruptions, security incidents, machine problems and the final distribution of seats are not yet known.
No claim about winners, party performance or the eventual chief minister should be treated as established until Comelec and the appropriate canvassing bodies release verified results.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for Comelec advisories during the voting period, verified reports of any election-related incidents, the close of polls, canvassing and the first reliable seat projections or official results.

The composition of the first elected parliament will determine the next phase of Bangsamoro governance, including the coalition or majority that can organize the chamber and choose the chief minister.

verificationNotes: Comelec's published election guidance establishes September 14, 2026 as election day and a 5 a.m. to 7 a.m. early-voting period for priority voters.
Inquirer.net reported during the current voting window that early voting had opened, establishing that the election had moved from a scheduled event to an event actually underway.
GMA News independently corroborates the election date, registered-voter count and parliamentary structure.
PNA independently corroborates Comelec's election-day procedures and early-voting schedule.
The PCO proclamation confirms September 14 as a special non-working day in BARMM to facilitate participation in the first parliamentary polls.
FMB News does not report turnout, winners, incidents or seat allocations that have not yet been verified.
